newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down 1.39 pct on political fears.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down 1.39 pct on political fears.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Friday on jitters over political instability after the resignations of three cabinet members ahead of a planned cabinet reshuffle, brokers said.
The weighted index ended down 116.48 points, or 1.39 percent, to 8,233.37, off an intraday low of 8,168.29.
Turnover was a heavy T$114.9 billion.
On Thursday, minister without portfolio Ma Ying-jeou, Interior Minister Lin Feng-cheng and Agriculture Council chairman Tjiu Mau-ying all resigned.

A planned move by opposition lawmakers to seek support for a motion asking President Lee Teng-hui to call for a complete cabinet reshuffle and to replace Premier Lien Chan increased uncertainty, brokers said.
Late on Friday morning, Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party blocked an attempt by opposition lawmakers to raise the motion in parliament.
Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee said instability would continue until the completion of the planned reshuffle eased people's worries.
The most heavily weighted financials plunged 2.29 percent. Rubbers, cements, plastics and transports all fell sharply.

But electronics rose 1.65 percent to help support the market. Chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$109.5 and another chipmaker United Microelectronics gained T$3 to T$73.5.
Notebook computer maker Inventec surged T$22 to T$375.
"Investors are hungry for semiconductor and notebook computer shares because of their expected sound sales and profit outlook in coming quarters," Lee said.
Despite the political worries, brokers said they did not expect any sharp falls ahead.
"Many expect the government to likely issue certain bullish news to help support the market, so a consolidation is more likely before the political uncertainty is over," Lee said.
A 8,200-8,300 range was seen for Saturday.
